Title (English)*: Medical outdoor patient Appointment system using Emerging Technology
Title (Bangla): মেডিকেল আউটডোর পেশেন্ট অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট সিস্টেম ইউজিং ইমার্জিং টেকনোলজি
Summary (English)*: A technology-enabled outpatient appointment system designed to reduce long patient waiting times and improve utilization of healthcare facilities in Bangladesh. Patients can obtain appointments through a mobile app, web-based system, toll-free/feature-phone service, SMS, or spot appointment. The proposed system uses AI/machine learning, patient information, GPS/location data, and patient-flow information to recommend suitable nearby healthcare facilities and departments. It also supports referral-based appointments, digital payments, notifications, and live token/queue updates.
Summary (Bangla): বাংলাদেশের স্বাস্থ্যসেবা প্রতিষ্ঠানে রোগীদের দীর্ঘ অপেক্ষার সময় কমানো এবং স্বাস্থ্যসেবা প্রতিষ্ঠানের কার্যকর ব্যবহার নিশ্চিত করার লক্ষ্যে একটি প্রযুক্তিনির্ভর বহির্বিভাগীয় অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট ব্যবস্থা। রোগীরা মোবাইল অ্যাপ, ওয়েবভিত্তিক সিস্টেম, টোল-ফ্রি/ফিচার ফোন সেবা, এসএমএস অথবা স্পট অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্টের মাধ্যমে সেবা নিতে পারবেন। প্রস্তাবিত সিস্টেমটি রোগীর তথ্য, অবস্থান, GPS এবং রোগীর প্রবাহের তথ্য ব্যবহার করে AI/মেশিন লার্নিংয়ের মাধ্যমে উপযুক্ত নিকটবর্তী স্বাস্থ্যসেবা প্রতিষ্ঠান ও বিভাগ সুপারিশ করবে। এতে রেফারেল অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট, ডিজিটাল পেমেন্ট, নোটিফিকেশন এবং লাইভ টোকেন/কিউ আপডেটের ব্যবস্থাও থাকবে।
Problem Statement*: Government health facilities in Bangladesh largely use manual and paper-based appointment systems, forcing patients to wait in long queues for serials and consultations. The proposal cites a mean waiting time of 2.42 hours in a tertiary-level hospital. Long waits reduce patient satisfaction and quality of care and increase pressure on hospital staff. Patients also tend to bypass lower-level facilities and seek specialist care at tertiary hospitals, causing overcrowding at tertiary facilities while primary and secondary facilities remain underutilized.
Proposed Solution*: Develop an integrated outpatient appointment platform accessible through mobile app, web, toll-free/feature-phone service, SMS, and spot counters. The system will use AI/machine learning, patient data, GPS/location, and current patient-flow information to recommend appropriate healthcare facilities and departments. It will integrate referrals, appointment confirmation, payment, reporting-time notifications, and real-time token/queue tracking.
Objectives: Reduce outpatient waiting time; reduce unnecessary overcrowding at tertiary hospitals; improve utilization of primary and secondary healthcare facilities; enable remote appointment booking; guide patients toward appropriate facilities/departments; integrate referrals with appointments; reduce unnecessary human involvement in appointment processing; provide real-time queue information; improve patient satisfaction and healthcare service quality.
Key Features: Online registration; online appointment; mobile app and web access; toll-free/feature-phone appointment; SMS appointment; spot appointment; structured symptom/problem questions; AI/ML-based facility and department recommendation; nearby facility suggestions; GPS-based distance/time calculation; referral-code-based appointments; reporting-time notifications; live token/current queue updates; mobile notifications; digital payment through mobile banking/mobile balance; bilingual Bangla and English interface; database backup; integration/API with health information systems.
Target Beneficiaries: Outpatients in Bangladesh, including patients without smartphones/computers; referred patients; doctors; hospital attendants/staff; government primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare facilities.
Impact: Expected to reduce outpatient waiting times, improve patient satisfaction and quality of care, reduce pressure on healthcare staff, save productive time for patients/doctors/attendants, reduce overcrowding at tertiary hospitals, and improve utilization of lower-level healthcare facilities.

The referral system will improve patient's compliance, quality of treatment and ensure proper utilization of all tiers of health care facilities.
Summary (Bangla): বাংলাদেশের কমিউনিটি ক্লিনিক থেকে শুরু করে ইউনিয়ন পর্যায়ের স্বাস্থ্যকেন্দ্র, উপজেলা স্বাস্থ্য কমপ্লেক্স, জেলা হাসপাতাল, মেডিকেল কলেজ হাসপাতাল ও বিশেষায়িত হাসপাতাল পর্যন্ত বিভিন্ন স্তরের স্বাস্থ্যসেবা প্রতিষ্ঠানকে ডিজিটালভাবে সংযুক্ত করার জন্য একটি কাঠামোবদ্ধ অনলাইন সফটওয়্যারভিত্তিক রেফারেল ব্যবস্থা। এটি কাগজভিত্তিক রেফারেল ব্যবস্থার পরিবর্তে রেফারকারী ও রেফারকৃত প্রতিষ্ঠানের মধ্যে দ্বিমুখী যোগাযোগ, প্রয়োজনীয় বিশেষজ্ঞ ও চিকিৎসাসুবিধার ভিত্তিতে উপযুক্ত হাসপাতাল নির্বাচন, জরুরি রোগীর আগাম নোটিফিকেশন ও অ্যাম্বুলেন্স সমন্বয়, সাধারণ রোগীর স্বয়ংক্রিয় অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট এবং DGHS-এর DHIS2, HRM ও Shared Health Record-এর সঙ্গে সমন্বয় করবে।
Problem Statement*: Bangladesh has a vast network of health facilities from ward level (community clinic) to national level (specialized and medical college hospitals). However, a structured referral system is not being followed. The present patient referral system is paper-based; referral protocol is often not maintained; identifying the right referral hospital with necessary facilities is challenging; there is no communication or coordination between referring and referred facilities; tertiary hospitals manage more patients than their capacity while primary health care facilities are underutilized.
Objectives: Improve patient's compliance, quality of treatment and proper utilization of all tiers of health care facilities; strengthen the referral mechanism.
Key Features: Structured referral system; forward referral; downward referral; interdepartmental referral; online software-based referral; SMS-based referral option for emergencies; two-way communication between referring and referred facilities; linkage with DHIS2, HRM, Shared Health Record and other hospital automation software; immediate notification to referred facilities; ambulance assistance; automatic appointment for routine cases; smartphone and laptop/desktop support; automatic referral register; secure data storage at MIS, DGHS; clinical triage protocol; consideration of patient's convenience and distance.
Target Beneficiaries: Patients; CHCPs; SACMO/HA/FWA; physicians; other relevant personnel; community clinics; union sub centers/family welfare centers; upazila health complexes; district hospitals; medical college hospitals; specialized hospitals.
Impact: Patients receive optimal care at the appropriate level and not unnecessarily costly; hospital facilities are used optimally and cost-effectively; clients who most need specialist services can access them in a timely way; primary health services are well utilized and their reputation is enhanced; urgent cases get best coordinated and safe treatment; workload of health care staff is reduced; the system will be sustainable and can be scaled up.

Summary (English)*: Doctor Connect is a digital referral and specialist appointment system designed to connect community clinics and primary healthcare centers with appropriate specialist doctors and tertiary/private hospitals. Healthcare workers can enter a patient's condition by typing or voice-to-text, search for specialists based on specialization, availability, distance and cost, and book appointments on behalf of patients. Patients receive appointment information through SMS while doctors receive notifications. The platform also supports emergency referral preparation, electronic prescriptions, patient medical-history storage, queue/token management, and specialist referral coordination.
Summary (Bangla): চিকিৎসক সংযোগ একটি ডিজিটাল রেফারেল ও বিশেষজ্ঞ চিকিৎসক অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট ব্যবস্থা, যার মাধ্যমে কমিউনিটি ক্লিনিক ও প্রাথমিক চিকিৎসা কেন্দ্রকে উপযুক্ত বিশেষজ্ঞ চিকিৎসক এবং উচ্চতর/বেসরকারি হাসপাতালের সঙ্গে সংযুক্ত করা হবে। স্বাস্থ্যকর্মীরা রোগীর সমস্যার বিবরণ টাইপ করে অথবা ভয়েস-টু-টেক্সটের মাধ্যমে সিস্টেমে প্রদান করতে পারবেন। রোগের ধরন, বিশেষজ্ঞের দক্ষতা, প্রাপ্যতা, দূরত্ব ও খরচের ভিত্তিতে উপযুক্ত চিকিৎসক খুঁজে অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট বুক করা যাবে। রোগী এসএমএসে তথ্য পাবেন এবং চিকিৎসক অ্যাপে নোটিফিকেশন পাবেন। সিস্টেমে জরুরি রেফারেল, ডিজিটাল প্রেসক্রিপশন, রোগীর চিকিৎসা ইতিহাস সংরক্ষণ এবং কিউ/টোকেন ব্যবস্থাপনাও থাকবে।
Problem Statement*: Healthcare workers at community clinics and primary healthcare centers often lack sufficient information to identify the appropriate specialist for patients with complex illnesses, causing delays in treatment. Receiving specialists may not know in advance when a referred patient will arrive or have access to the patient's medical history. Patients may also travel unnecessarily to distant cities despite suitable specialists being available nearby, wasting time and money. For critically ill patients referred to emergency departments, hospitals and doctors may not receive advance information necessary to prepare appropriate care, potentially contributing to severe outcomes including loss of life.
Proposed Solution*: Develop a mobile application-based referral platform connecting specialist doctor profiles with primary healthcare centers, hospitals and doctors. Healthcare workers enter patient conditions through text or voice-to-text, after which the system identifies possible specialists and provides their location and appointment availability. The healthcare worker can book an appropriate specialist appointment, send appointment information to the patient, and notify the receiving doctor. Emergency departments can receive advance referrals, doctors can create prescriptions through the application, and patient histories are stored in a database for future treatment.
Objectives: Improve referrals from community/primary healthcare to specialist and tertiary care; help healthcare workers identify appropriate specialists; reduce treatment delays; reduce unnecessary travel and patient expenses; enable advance appointment booking; improve communication between referring facilities and receiving doctors/hospitals; prepare hospitals for emergency referrals; maintain patient medical histories; improve continuity of care; and establish an efficient digital referral pathway.
Key Features: Specialist doctor profile database; specialist search by specialization, availability, distance and cost; text-based patient information entry; voice-to-text input; digital referral; specialist appointment booking; patient SMS notifications; doctor app notifications; emergency referral alerts; digital/electronic prescriptions; prescription printing; patient medical-history database; digital token system; queue management and updates; doctor availability tracking.
Target Beneficiaries: Patients, particularly those using community clinics and primary healthcare facilities; community clinic and primary healthcare workers; specialist doctors; hospitals and emergency departments; patients requiring specialist or tertiary-level referrals.
Impact: Expected to reduce delays in specialist treatment, unnecessary travel and patient expenses; improve referral accuracy and continuity of care; enable receiving doctors to access relevant patient information; improve preparedness for emergency referrals; and make specialist healthcare more accessible through coordinated digital referrals.

Title (English)*: Sustainable E-traceability system for exportable fruits and vegetables of Bangladesh
Title (Bangla): সাসটেইনেবল ই-ট্রেসেবিলিটি সিস্টেম ফর এক্সপোর্টেবল ফ্রুটস অ্যান্ড ভেজিটেবলস অব বাংলাদেশ
Summary (English)*: A digital e-traceability system designed to digitize the value chain of selected fruits and vegetables for exporters, enabling real-time tracking of farmers, farms, inputs, cultivation, harvesting, procurement, product movement, processing, packaging and distribution. The system aims to provide transparent and trusted product information to exporters, importers and consumers
Summary (Bangla): রপ্তানিযোগ্য নির্বাচিত ফল ও সবজির সম্পূর্ণ মূল্য শৃঙ্খল ডিজিটালাইজ করার জন্য প্রস্তাবিত একটি ই-ট্রেসেবিলিটি ব্যবস্থা, যার মাধ্যমে কৃষক, খামার, কৃষি উপকরণ, চাষাবাদ, ফসল সংগ্রহ, ক্রয়, পণ্য স্থানান্তর, প্রক্রিয়াজাতকরণ ও প্যাকেজিংসহ বিভিন্ন ধাপের তথ্য সংরক্ষণ ও ট্র্যাক করা হবে।
Problem Statement*: Existing agricultural traceability and record-keeping processes rely heavily on manual, paper-based systems, resulting in cumbersome data collection and duplication of work. There is no real-time overview of data, inadequate traceability across agricultural production and supply chains, insufficient transparency in financial transactions, and inadequate monitoring of farmer training. These limitations create challenges for meeting increasing food-safety, traceability and market-compliance requirements in international markets.
Proposed Solution*: Develop a comprehensive digital e-traceability platform for fruits and vegetables, consisting of mobile and web-based systems. The platform will digitize the value chain, create farmer and farm databases, manage agricultural input and financial transactions, track production and movement of products, use QR codes for farm-to-fork traceability, and integrate blockchain technology for supply-chain management.
Objectives: 1. Develop a mobile app and web-based data management system. 2. Create databases for contract farmers and farms. 3. Manage distribution of agricultural inputs and cash advances. 4. Improve farm-to-fork traceability through QR codes. 5. Integrate blockchain technology into the supply-chain platform. 6. Build capacity of target users. 7. Provide training and support to exporter staff
Key Features: Farmer enrollment; farm enrollment and GPS mapping; cultivation and input distribution tracking; farm inspection; crop harvest recording; procurement and batch/lot tracking; product transfer and inventory tracking; collection-center reception; processing and export packaging records; QR-code-based traceability; dashboard and MIS reporting; Excel/PDF report export.
Target Beneficiaries: Agricultural exporters; contract farmers; field staff; aggregators; processing/collection centers; importers; international-market actors; consumers. The system particularly supports exporters and their farmers.

Title (English)*: Tracer: One stop solution for traceable production pipeline
Title (Bangla): ট্রেসার: ওয়ান স্টপ সলিউশন ফর ট্রেসেবল প্রোডাকশন পাইপলাইন
Summary (English)*: A blockchain-based web application exposing APIs that allow enterprises across multiple industries to register, define their own traceability pipelines, and record immutable supply-chain data on the Government of Bangladesh Traceability Platform. Rather than building industry-specific systems, Tracer provides an abstraction layer between blockchain technicalities and production-pipeline requirements, enabling firms to configure agents, processes, sensors and activities to their own regulatory standards.
Summary (Bangla): ট্রেসার একটি ব্লকচেইনভিত্তিক ওয়েব অ্যাপ্লিকেশন, যা এপিআই-এর মাধ্যমে বিভিন্ন শিল্পখাতের প্রতিষ্ঠানকে বাংলাদেশ সরকারের ট্রেসেবিলিটি প্ল্যাটফর্মে যুক্ত হয়ে সরবরাহ-শৃঙ্খলের তথ্য অপরিবর্তনীয়ভাবে সংরক্ষণের সুযোগ দেবে। প্রতিটি খাতের জন্য পৃথক ব্যবস্থা তৈরির পরিবর্তে এই সমাধানটি ব্লকচেইনের কারিগরি জটিলতা ও উৎপাদন পাইপলাইনের চাহিদার মধ্যে একটি বিমূর্ত স্তর তৈরি করে, যাতে প্রতিটি প্রতিষ্ঠান নিজস্ব বিধিবিধান অনুযায়ী এজেন্ট, প্রক্রিয়া, সেন্সর ও কার্যক্রম নির্ধারণ করে নিজেদের ট্রেসেবিলিটি পাইপলাইন গড়ে তুলতে পারে। নিবন্ধন সম্পন্ন হলে প্রতিষ্ঠানকে এপিআই কী প্রদান করা হবে, যার মাধ্যমে তারা আইওটি সেন্সর, ড্যাশবোর্ড ও অ্যাপ্লিকেশন সংযুক্ত করতে পারবে। ব্লকচেইনের তথ্য সবার জন্য উন্মুক্ত থাকলেও কেবল যাচাইকৃত প্রতিষ্ঠানের দেওয়া তথ্যই বৈধ হিসেবে গণ্য হবে।
Problem Statement*: Export buyers increasingly demand transparency and ESG compliance, but traceability digitisation efforts in Bangladesh stall after the pilot phase. Two causes are identified: (i) systems are designed for a single industry, and regulatory regimes differ by sector (FIQC/DoF/BFFEA/BQSP-UNIDO for shrimp; LWG for leather); and (ii) new traceability systems are incompatible with the internal management systems large facilities already operate, forcing duplicate data entry.
Proposed Solution*: A web application built on blockchain that issues APIs to verified firms. Registration occurs in two stages: the firm defines its own traceability pipeline (agents, processes, sensors, activities), then a regulatory authority verifies the firm's existence and capability. No hardcoded data storage structure is used, enabling cross-industry compatibility, while schema constraints are applied at the intra-industry level based on the pipeline definition. Registered firms receive an API key for connecting IoT sensors, dashboards and applications. All data is open to read, but only data submitted by verified firms is treated as valid.
Key Features: Two-stage firm registration with regulatory verification; user-defined traceability pipeline; schema-free blockchain storage with intra-industry constraints; API key issuance for IoT/dashboard/app development; cryptographic signing of each data record; validation to prevent data inconsistency and corruption; rules tracking format changes; industry-created dashboards; permissioned structure (Hyperledger Fabric referenced) allowing stakeholder correction of erroneous transactions.
Target Beneficiaries: Export-oriented industries (shrimp/frozen foods, leather cited); farmers, depot operators, auction centres, processing plants; regulatory and audit agencies (DoF, FIQC, BFFEA, LWG); Government of Bangladesh; international buyers and end consumers.

Summary (English)*: An IoT-based ecosystem for measuring urban water consumption, monitoring water quality and reducing wastage. Flow, level, TDS and TSS sensors connect wirelessly to a custom-designed THiNK IoT Hub, which feeds a cloud platform providing consumer billing, real-time quality readings, fault detection and peer-to-peer usage comparison. Consumers access daily and monthly usage, water quality parameters and bill payment through a mobile app; WASA administrators monitor zone-level consumption, billing status and faulty devices through a web dashboard. A gamification layer (Leader Board and Super Hero models) encourages households to compete on conservation. The design accommodates existing plumbing without modification and has been validated through a working proof of concept.

Summary (English)*: Upgrade residential water meters into smart meters in order to avail Advance Metering Infrastructure (AMI) facilities for monitoring, flow-shedding, billing and controlling each individual zone's consumers' water consumption remotely from zone-wise AMI control rooms. The proposal is segmented into three areas: arrangement according to system architecture; user-friendly interfaces for easy operation; and the benefits of an online pre-payment AMI system. Household meters communicate through Pulse Output, GSM, M-Bus or RF, via a Data Concentrator Unit (DCU) and mobile network/internet, to an AMI server, supporting automatic bill generation and payment through mobile app, bank and POS.

Problem Statement*: The water supply analysis and billing platform for management of the domestic water supply sector has been considered a challenge in terms of providing sufficient information related to urban users' water consumption footprint.
Proposed Solution*: Upgrade residential water meters into smart meters to avail AMI facilities for remote monitoring, flow-shedding, billing and control of each zone's consumers from respective AMI control rooms. Household water meters connect via Pulse Output (to GSM/SMS/RF), GSM, M-Bus or RF; M-Bus and RF route through a Data Concentrator Unit (DCU) to the internet and on to the server. Meters with AMR provision transmit over GSM/GPRS/RF through the mobile network to the AMI server room and head office, enabling automatic bill generation, bill receiving and payment via mobile app, and payment through bank/POS. The system includes an end-user portal (login, admin panel with consumer particulars, raw data list of date-wise present unit and consumption, payment history, and a billing screen showing present reading, last unit paid, consumption, VAT 15%, service charge 5% and ground total due with an online payment option).
Objectives: Enable monitoring, flow-shedding, billing and controlling of individual zone consumers' water consumption remotely from AMI control rooms; make water distribution to the end user more efficient, transparent and cost-effective; grow public awareness by restricting excess water wastage through a transparent billing system and by acknowledging individuals' daily water consumption.
Key Features: Billing with the utility's applied tariff policy from the online server with a single tap; prepaid/postpaid mode switchable by the server; anti-storage, insufficient-water warning and self-defined overdraft; anti-tamper detection and log (open case, open battery cover, tilt); event log (top-up, valve open/close, leakage detection); data security by encryption, AES-128, STS and communication security; programmable emergency credit (holiday hour, friendly hour); SMS to customer mobile based on credit balance; AMR and load control through two-way communication; reduced human resource requirement for billing without accessing the metering point; billing accuracy through online checking on the AMI server using a smart mobile phone; hardware-independent software compatible with any AMR water meter with open communication protocol; low-cost per-user consumption monitoring and billing using a single DCU covering a 1 km radius.
Target Beneficiaries: Beneficiaries	Domestic/residential water consumers (individual households, multi-storey buildings and industrial premises as shown in the architecture), the water utility (DWASA head office and zone-wise AMI control rooms), and the general public.
Impact: More efficient, transparent and cost-effective water distribution to end users; increased public awareness and reduced water wastage; transparent bill generation and acknowledgement of daily individual consumption; savings in human resources for billing; improved billing accuracy.

Summary (English)*: A water footprint data analytics platform for the textile and leather industries. Hall-effect flow sensors and data loggers link via Bluetooth/WiFi mesh or LoRaWAN to a mother communication gateway, which sends data to the cloud over 2G/GSM/WiFi/LoRaWAN using MQTT. Water quality data (BOD, COD, TDS, pH) is taken from existing ETP sensors and compared with the ETP's set parameters. A web dashboard (Python backend, Vue.js or React.js frontend) shows hourly usage, recycle, reuse and wastage, a 7-day consumption report, water treatment values, a GIS map heatmap, and a peer-to-peer comparison leaderboard. Offered as a SaaS monthly subscription with no upfront cost.

Problem Statement*: Declining groundwater levels and deteriorating river water quality have reached alarming levels in Bangladesh. Textile and leather — the most prominent industrial sectors and source of the majority of export earnings — are also the biggest annual water consumers. Textile consumption starts at yarn scouring and dyeing, and peaks in knit and woven composite factories where grey fabrics are bleached, dyed and washed; in leather, water is used in processing, dyeing and final assembly. Cited usage per product: t-shirt 2,700 L, jeans 3,400 L, leather jackets 30,000 L, leather shoes 8,000 L. Understanding the footprint requires starting with composite factories to establish usage in scouring, bleaching and dyeing, recycling of used water, reuse of recycled water, and water unable to be reused after recycling.
Proposed Solution*: Hall-effect flow sensors (cheaper than ultrasound-based) across factory zones such as dyeing and washing, with sensor count depending on the factory's schematic design. A mother communication gateway connects up to 5 meters via Bluetooth/WiFi mesh or LoRaWAN and transfers data via 2G/GSM/WiFi/LoRaWAN. ETP-based sensors measure BOD, COD, TDS and pH of recycled or treated water against set ETP parameters; where possible this data is collected as digital signals from the existing ETP control panel, avoiding extra sensors. Data reaches the cloud via MQTT with an MQTT broker, requiring less bandwidth and power. Dashboard: Python backend, Vue.js or React.js frontend, with peer-to-peer comparison and leaderboard. Data loggers and gateways are produced locally; data is stored in the company's local cloud centre on a SaaS basis, with setup, maintenance and repair by the company using local resources and manpower. LoRaWAN in EPZ areas (the company would build its own network, as none exists in Bangladesh), 2G-GSM elsewhere; 3G/4G avoided due to unstable in-factory coverage and cost, though the modular device supports future 3G/4G and NB-IoT integration and runs on AC/DC or solar batteries with long-time backup.
Key Features: Hall-effect flow sensors connected to valves; data loggers on Bluetooth/WiFi mesh or LoRaWAN; mother gateway for up to 5 meters; MQTT cloud transfer with low bandwidth and power use; ETP quality monitoring (BOD, COD, TDS, pH); dashboard with hourly usage, recycle, reuse and wastage split by bleaching, dyeing and washing, 7-day consumption report, water treatment value, GIS heatmap; peer-to-peer comparison and industry leaderboard with company-level drill-down; modular devices for any OS or communication module; AC/DC and solar operation with power backup; locally made loggers and gateways giving control over data security and privacy; tier-3 data centre in Mohakhali; SaaS subscription with no upfront cost.
Target Beneficiaries: Textile and leather industry factories (knit and woven composite factories; companies shown on the industry leaderboard)

Summary (English)*: A phygital platform combining on-premises access to affordable essentials with financial wellness services for industrial workers. On-site retail stores inside factories and industrial zones are paired with a digital platform offering credit, savings and insurance. Services include interest-free credit up to 30% of salary in advance on 2,200+ discounted products, near-zero interest purposeful payday and short-term loans of 1–6 months, appliance instalments without collateral via automatic payroll deduction, small-ticket formal savings, and free health insurance worth $200 with life coverage worth $250 earned through purchase points. Retail staff provide digital literacy support. The goal is 1M workers empowered by 2030 through 150 shops and 13.4m USD in discounts.

Problem Statement*: In Bangladesh, industrial workers support their families on wages barely sufficient for basic needs, without access to affordable credit and groceries: 96% lack savings and 90.8% cannot afford essential groceries and healthcare without falling into debt. Globally, 2.1 billion blue collar workers struggle to access affordable essential goods, healthcare and financial services. Financial exclusion takes the form of limited access to formal banking, high-cost credit and predatory lending, and a lack of appropriate financial products; food and essentials challenges include overpriced local options, time-consuming commutes to affordable stores, and trust deficits in quality and authenticity. The paradox is that full-time workers essential to economic growth remain trapped in low savings and debt, producing reduced productivity, poor health outcomes and limited social mobility.
Proposed Solution*: A phygital model — physical plus digital. Physical presence: on-site retail stores within factories and industrial zones, face-to-face service and immediate access, better worker engagement to tailor services, and digital literacy support from retail staff. Digital innovation: integrated financial services (credit, savings, insurance), free health insurance for loyal customers, data-driven personalized financial solutions, and a secure, easy-to-use platform.
Key Features: Interest-free credit of up to 30% of salary in advance for discounted purchases from 2,200+ products; near-zero interest purposeful payday and short-term loans of 1–6 months; appliance instalments via app without collateral with automatic payroll deductions; affordable small-ticket formal savings; free health insurance worth $200 and life coverage worth $250 through purchase points. Differentiators: phygital integration of essential retail and financial services; cost-free credit adding no cost to workers; high impact and low default built on trust and essential needs; comprehensive wellbeing beyond finance. Compared in the deck against Roshod and wagely across fair-price retail shops, grocery credit, instalment purchase, payday loans and savings.
Target Beneficiaries: Blue collar/industrial workers in Bangladesh (2.1 billion globally; 7M industrial workers in Bangladesh, 90% with limited access to affordable essential goods and credit)
Impact: 9/10 customers report improved quality of life; $1.2mn in customer savings on groceries to date; $12M in embedded finance deployed; 78% of customers report improvements in their financial situation; 20K+ customers received a free health card; 43% female customers, with all products and services designed with female customers in mind and internal gender inclusion policies based on 2X criteria assessment. A 60Decibels impact study is referenced.

The machine is designed to address oxygen shortages among COVID-19 patients by producing medical-grade oxygen on-site. It has a 5-liter-per-minute oxygen production capacity with 92%–98% purity.

The system uses an oil-free compressor to draw atmospheric air through an air filter and compress it into a zeolite cylinder. Through the Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) process, the zeolite separates oxygen from nitrogen. The produced oxygen is stored in a reserve cylinder and supplied to patients through a flowmeter. The machine can provide oxygen to more than one patient simultaneously.
